- Model tends to overestimate prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early or too high, then underestimates the subsequent correction or mean reversion.
- Model underestimates true outcomes in the latter half of the forecast window, particularly after a strong upward move.
- Forecast shows persistent lag in capturing true price momentum, especially when prices are trending upward.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values when recent history includes strong upward momentum, and underestimates when momentum is weak or reversing.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes, then fails to adjust downward quickly enough — correction is delayed or insufficient.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled; model often fails to recognize that prices will revert to historical averages after a spike.
- Forecast tends to be overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then becomes overly pessimistic in the last 10–15 days.
